title: Dance in the Vampire Bund
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Mina Tepes, the ancient ruler of all vampires who has the body of a young girl, pays off Japan's national debt to win a special district, the Bund, off the coast of Tokyo as a haven for her people. With her werewolf bodyguard Akira, she reveals vampires to the world and defends the Bund from fearful humans, terrorists and extremist vampire factions.
life_message: Coexistence between peoples is worth fighting for, and devotion to one's sworn protector is the highest bond.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Mina answers attacks on her people with force (Wikipedia).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Mina rules the Bund as sovereign under her own law.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Vampire clans and lineage loyalty drive the politics.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Princess-ruler of all vampires with a sworn bodyguard (Wikipedia).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Ancient vampire covenant combined with modern finance and media.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Security of a besieged people is the central concern.

folkways.japan: Set off the coast of Tokyo; Japan's government and media debate accepting outsiders, a theme that echoes Japanese discussion of immigration (described, not judged).

delivery.evidence: Fandom Post finds the story superficial and not moralizing; coexistence theme carried by plot (Wikipedia).
delivery.note: Fear on both sides is shown as the obstacle, with Mina's vision presented as the hopeful path.

winners_losers: Mina and Akira defend the Bund against human and vampire extremists; sympathy goes to coexistence and to the bond between sovereign and protector.
